title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 94 (Place of keeping and inspection of registers)

content.overview: Registers under section 88 and copies of the annual return under section 92 must be kept at the registered office. They may be kept elsewhere in India if more than one-tenth of Members reside there and a special resolution approves. The specified registers, indices and returns are open to inspection during business hours; eligible holders may inspect and take extracts without charge, while copies are available on prescribed fees, subject to prescribed exclusions. Refusal attracts a daily penalty capped at ₹1,00,000 and the Central Government may order immediate inspection or extracts.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 94 (Place of keeping and inspection of registers, returns, etc.). Registers required under section 88 and copies of the annual return under section 92 must be kept at the registered office. They may be kept at another place in India where more than one-tenth of the Members entered in the register reside, if approved by special resolution at a general meeting. Except when lawfully closed, the registers, indices and copies of returns are open for inspection during business hours: Members, debenture-holders, other security holders and beneficial owners inspect without charge; other persons pay prescribed fees. The persons identified in subsection (3) may take extracts without charge or require copies on payment of prescribed fees. Prescribed particulars, including address/registered address, email ID, Unique Identification Number and PAN, are excluded from inspection/extract/copy under the applicable rules. If inspection, an extract or a copy is refused, subsection (4) imposes a penalty of ₹1,000 for every day the refusal/default continues, capped at ₹1,00,000, on the company and every officer in default. Under subsection (5), the Central Government may direct immediate inspection or allow the extract to be taken forthwith. Legal verification remains open.

sections.heading: Place of keeping
sections.body: Registers required under section 88 and copies of the annual return filed under section 92 are kept at the registered office. They may also be kept at another place in India where more than one-tenth of the Members entered in the register reside, if approved by a special resolution passed at a general meeting.

sections.heading: Inspection
sections.body: Except when closed under the Act, the registers and indices and copies of returns are open for inspection during business hours. A Member, debenture-holder, other security holder or beneficial owner may inspect without fee; another person pays the prescribed fee.

sections.heading: Extracts and copies
sections.body: A Member, debenture-holder, other security holder, beneficial owner or other person may take extracts without fee or require a copy of the register, entries or return on payment of prescribed fees. Prescribed personal particulars, including address/registered address, email ID, Unique Identification Number and PAN, are not available for inspection, extracts or copies under the applicable rules.

sections.heading: Penalty for refusal
sections.body: If inspection, an extract or a copy required under section 94 is refused, the company and every officer in default are liable, for each such default, to a penalty of ₹1,000 for every day during which the refusal/default continues, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000.

sections.heading: Immediate remedy
sections.body: The Central Government may by order direct immediate inspection of the document or direct that the required extract be allowed to be taken forthwith.

hypotheticals.question: A company refuses a Member's inspection request for the register of members. What consequences may follow under section 94?
hypotheticals.analysis: Check whether the register is covered and whether the request is within the statutory inspection right. hypotheticals.question: May an ordinary member of the public obtain every field in the register of members?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Although section 94 permits inspection and copies subject to prescribed fees and rights, prescribed particulars such as addresses, email IDs, Unique Identification Numbers and PAN are excluded under the applicable rules. Check the current rules for the exact excluded fields.

distinctions.title: Inspection entitlement and copy entitlement
distinctions.left: Eligible holders may inspect covered registers and returns during business hours, with no fee for the listed holder categories.
distinctions.right: Copies may be requested on prescribed fees; prescribed personal particulars remain excluded.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming registers may be kept at any location once a special resolution is passed.
misconceptions.correction: The alternative location must be in India where more than one-tenth of the Members reside, and a special resolution must approve it.

misconceptions.trap: Treating all inspection/copy requests as free or allowing all personal fields to be disclosed.
misconceptions.correction: The fee and entitlement depend on the requester category, and prescribed particulars are excluded from inspection/extract/copy.

misconceptions.trap: Omitting the continuing daily penalty or the Central Government's immediate-inspection power.
misconceptions.correction: Subsections (4) and (5) state those separate consequences and remedies.
